content_sections.heading: About NZP Associate (Legal)-B
content_sections.text: The National Zoological Park, located on Mathura Road in New Delhi, is a Subordinate Office of the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change. Through this circular, NZP is engaging one Associate (Legal)-B on a contract basis to assist it with its legal issues and court cases, including matters before the Supreme Court of India, the High Courts and the National Green Tribunal (NGT).

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Bachelor's Degree in Law (LL.B) or equivalent from a recognized University and/or Institute in India, recognized by the Bar Council of India. Experience of more than two (2) years and upto three (3) years. Enrolled as an Advocate with the Bar Council of India or any State Bar Council, under the provisions of The Advocates Act, 1961. Experience of handling cases related to environment, forests, biodiversity, wildlife, establishment matters, contract-related matters etc. in a Government of India or State Government Department/Board. Possessing a Diploma/Certificate of specialization in related subjects/fields from a recognized University/Institution. Preference would be given to: candidates who scored 60% (Sixty Percent) and above marks/CGPA equivalent in the LL.B exam; candidates who studied in a full-time LLB course; candidates who scored 60% (Sixty Percent) and above marks/CGPA equivalent in the LL.M. The maximum age limit for engagement of Associates (Legal-B) is 50 years. The application form asks whether the applicant is within the age limit of 50 years on the last date of receipt of application. The notice does not mention any category-wise age relaxation; it states only that the Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change may, by order and for recorded reasons, relax any provision of these guidelines where necessary or expedient. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the Associate (Legal)-B post.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Remuneration: Rs. 50,000.00 (Fifty Thousand only) per month. Annual increment: between 0% and 10% (including 2% weightage for updation of the LIMBS portal and Legal Repository of National Zoological Park, if any), depending on quality of performance, as determined by the Competent Authority on a case-to-case basis. Incentive: Rs. 1500/- per appearance before the Hon'ble National Green Tribunal in pro forma cases; the maximum incentive per case shall be not more than Rs. 15,000/-. No other allowances: Associates (Legal) are not entitled to allowances such as Dearness Allowance, residential telephone facility, residential accommodation, personal staff, CGHS or medical reimbursement. Tenure: initial engagement up to three years (1+1+1), subject to satisfactory performance. Continuation beyond three years, for up to two more years, will be considered on a case-to-case basis with the approval of the Competent Authority. The maximum tenure is up to five years. Nature of post: temporary and purely contractual; no request for promotion will be entertained. 1.5 days of leave after completion of each month of service, accruing on a completed-month, pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Accumulation beyond the calendar year/extension period may not be allowed; leave cannot be claimed as a right and may be refused or revoked in the public interest. No leave encashment; unspent leave lapses when the notice period begins. Absence beyond entitled leave leads to a proportionate deduction from the consolidated fee; absence of up to one month may be treated as without remuneration. Women Associates (Legal-B) may be eligible for maternity leave as per the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017. TA, DA and hotel accommodation for official work as per SR 190. Outstation travel: train in 2nd AC, taxi on actual basis within the city, food bill/stationery charges up to Rs. 500/- per day and hotel charges Rs. 2,000/- per day on production of proper receipt, subject to actual expenditure. Travel within Headquarter: taxi on actual basis within the city where NZP is located, and stationery charges/food bill up to Rs. 200 per day, subject to actual expenditure. Under exceptional circumstances, domestic travel at Government expense may be allowed with the approval of the Competent Authority in public interest.

content_sections.heading: NZP Associate (Legal)-B Job Description
content_sections.text: As per the Terms of Reference (Annexure-II), the Associate (Legal) will assist NZP in handling and monitoring all legal issues and judicial cases and in preparing material for briefing the Ld. Attorney General, Ld. Solicitor General, Additional and Assistant Solicitor Generals and Central Government Standing Counsels. The tasks listed are: Assisting NZP on all matters wherever legal issues are involved. Handling issues related to law for effective implementation of related laws and framework, and cases related to establishment matters. Assisting in court cases before the Supreme Court of India, various High Courts, the NGT and its Benches and other courts and judicial forums. Drafting and filing affidavits, applications, review appeals, special leave petitions, transfer petitions and para-wise replies. Attending/appearing in court proceedings on dates of hearing, as and when required. Pro-actively monitoring legal issues and judicial cases and assisting in briefing the law officers and counsels. Assisting the Government Counsels during hearings. Maintaining status reports of ongoing court cases and tracking dates of next hearing to alert the officers concerned. Following up all cases and case files and tracking court hearings. Coordinating with State Government officials, other Ministries/Departments and MoEF&CC on legal matters. Liaising with Central Government legal counsels and empanelled counsels of MoEF&CC for NGT. Streamlining court cases and developing a more efficient legal monitoring system. Updating information/data in the LIMBS software of the Ministry of Law & Justice or any other NZP database. Conducting research on prevailing laws and assisting in answering RTI applications and Parliament Questions involving legal issues. Drafting and scrutinising tender documents and agreements with vendors or other institutions. Undertaking any other task assigned by the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: CEC members: Inspector General of Forests (Wildlife Division), MoEF&CC – Chairperson; Director, National Zoological Park – Member; Joint Director, Wildlife Division – Member. Shortlisted candidates will be called for interview through e-mail. The CEC shall recommend one suitable candidate along with one candidate as reserve. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the interview or joining.
